A couple of notes:

- The **Meeting Room 2** booking for the Coding Club on Saturday mornings has been moved to **Meeting Room 1** due to the room’s capacity. We had 38 children at the last session in November, and Room 2 only holds 30. Room 1 holds 50, so we should have enough space even if numbers grow.
- The **Storytime** sessions in the children’s area will continue as scheduled. No changes required.
- The **Teen Writers’ Group** will use the **Quiet Study Room** on Thursday afternoons. Please note the room has a lockable door, which we’ll need for the sessions as the group has requested privacy.

I’ve also updated the room booking spreadsheet on the shared drive, so please check that if you need a quick reference.

**Attendance reporting**

As we discussed, the end-of-year attendance report is due to the Regional Office by 19 December 2025. I’ve drafted the summary for the period 1 July to 30 November 2025, and I’ll circulate it for review by the end of this week. The report will include:

- Total program sessions held
- Total attendance across all programs
- Breakdown by age group (children, teens, adults)
- Breakdown by program type (storytime, coding, craft, book clubs, etc.)
- Notes on any significant trends or changes

I’ll need your input on the programs you’ve each run, so please send me your session counts and any comments by **12 December 2025**. I’ve attached a template to this email that you can fill in – it’s the same one we used for the mid-year report.

**Equipment update**

The feature worked well overall, though we did have a few teething issues with automated waitlist notifications going to the wrong email address – Liam has since fixed that.

The Python Basics series was the first time we’ve run a text-based coding program for this age group, and it was a clear success. Registrations filled within 48 hours of opening, and the waitlist grew to 23 names by the first session. This tells me there is real demand for structured, multi-week coding programs, not just one-off workshops.

- We had a few instances of participants sharing their login details, which caused some confusion with saved work. For the Autumn Session, we’ll need to set a clear expectation in the welcome email about not sharing logins.
